Subject: DPA redlines and SCCs mapping for EU deployment

Hi Irene —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Attaching the initial DPA redlines from our side (clarity_dpa_redlines_v1.docx) — primary asks below:

- We need to confirm whether Redwood will be listed as a "processor" only, and whether any "subprocessor" list will be captured in an annex (Clarity requires a fixed subprocessor list for the pilot).
- Clarify which party is responsible for cross-border exit data exports and whether an export addendum / transfer impact schedule will be provided.
- We tried to map the standard EU SCCs to the service flow; please see our suggested column headers in the attached SCCs worksheet.

Can you confirm who on your side will own the role matrix and whether you can provide encryption key custody detail for EU regions? Our security team has a quick questionnaire they may push within the next 48 hours.

Appreciate a timeline — ideally we'd have a DPA agreed (or a narrow open list) before contract signature on 2/2.

Thanks,

Irene — quick operational notes after looking at the SCCs workbook (I've attached a cleaned mapping):

- Pilot subprocessor list: we can include a closed list for the initial 90-day pilot (GPUs in us-west-2; logging to S3 in eu-west-1). Ops will commit to notifying Clarity 30 days before adding additional subprocessors, but we can't guarantee a permanent locked list post-pilot (need ongoing approval flow).
- Key custody: for the hosted offering we hold tenant-level encryption keys in a KMS we control; we can offer a BYOK option for Dedicated/Private. For EU-hosted keys, our KMS is region-bound and uses HSM-backed keys.
- Export responsibility: we propose Redwood be responsible for facilitating secure transfer (export process and technical export evidence), but Clarity remains controller for deciding the destination and for any regulatory notifications.

I added comments in sccs_mapping.xlsx with sequence numbers that map to the DPA clauses. See attachment: sccs_mapping.xlsx

Ben

Thanks Ben — helpful. From legal side:

- Processor vs controller: we'll accept being listed as "processor" in the DPA. However, we need limited exceptions for telemetry and aggregated metrics; propose carveout language that keeps data pseudonymized and limited to operational debugging.
- Subprocessor list: agree to the pilot-locked list for 90 days. Add: include a clause allowing CLAR to request an audit of the subprocessor list once per year.
- SCCs: replace the generic cross-border clause with the new EU SCC 2021 text and attach an SCC annex referencing our technical controls (we should not embed the entire mapping in the DPA, but link to an annex that can be updated under notice).
- Export addendum: I'll draft an export addendum template that specifies roles/steps for transfer and includes a line for KMS custody. Will circulate a redline by EOD Wednesday.

Also — suggest we send the revised DPA to Wilson & Co early so external counsel can confirm SCC alignment before we send final to Clarity.

Laura Bennett

Redwood Inference

Subject: Updated DPA + next steps (pilot subprocessor list + SCCs annex)

Marta / Wilson team —

Thanks for the detailed redlines. We've consolidated internal feedback and attached a revised DPA (clarity_dpa_revised_v2.docx) and an SCCs annex template that references operational mappings rather than embedding them. Key points agreed or proposed: 

- Processor designation: Redwood will be the processor. We will include a pseudonymous-telemetry carveout limited to debugging and service health; exact language is in §3.2 of the attached.
- Pilot subprocessor list: Redwood will provide a locked subprocessor list for the initial 90-day pilot. We will notify Clarity 30 days prior to any addition outside the pilot. Clarity may request an annual subprocessor audit (see §6.4).
- Export addendum: attached is a draft export addendum template. Operationally Redwood will facilitate secure export and provide transfer logs; Clarity (controller) will determine destination and carry out any regulatory notices.
- KMS/key custody: for the hosted pilot we will hold region-bound HSM-backed keys; if Clarity requires BYOK we can scope Dedicated/Private as separate line items in the order form.

Next steps: 
1) Laura will send a redline with exact SCC annex cross-references to Wilson & Co by EOD tomorrow.
2) Wilson & Co to confirm SCC template fit-for-purpose within 48 hours.
3) If SCCs are cleared, we will route the revised DPA + order form to procurement for final signature by subset owners (timeline: target 2/2).

DocuSign preview: https://www.docusign.com/links/clarity-dpa-2026
